scope: Corollary 6.5 (Singleton and ball compatibility) of the manuscript “Cycle--clique Ramsey numbers” (preprints/Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25-2026/Cycle-clique-Ramsey-numbers-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 189 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 366fc1d94b08e498), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider two options based at distinct vertices x, y ∈ X, with integer radius labels r, s ≥ −1. If r = s = −1, the two options are disjoint and anticomplete whenever xy / ∈ E(G). Otherwise, they are disjoint and anticomplete whenever all outside x–y paths relative to X with parameters 1 ≤ d ≤ r + s + 2 are forbidden.
